Task: do a real end-to-end re-run against /Users/jaxson/Downloads/codingprojects/support-agent-demo with a GOOD commit BEFORE R1 so all three regressions are in range (use the first commit `1b40b27`, or the latest commit before brief 6 `ec19917` if 1b40b27 fails the cases — verify with a quick eval first). Bad end = HEAD of the demo history at the commit just before the new tracing/flaky commits (5cee99b... check `git log`; use the commit where the three planted regressions are all present, and set DEMO_FLAKE=0 for the runs). Use the bad trace from the earlier run (e2dad5356ed1bc49c59bc0446442df54, case rw1) or generate fresh; neatlogs multi-span traces dead-letter (known backend issue, evidence/neatlogs-dlq-report.md), so span divergence will not work live — don't spend time on that; signature path is the focus. Rounds/eval-rounds smart vs plain, backoff events observed, any rate limiting. Commit the resulting reports into evidence/ (reports for each signature + a short evidence/rerun-summary.md with the numbers and caveats), update BUILD_LOG.md, push to origin main. Commit messages end with: Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>. # Large multi-feature tasks

When a request is big — multiple features, or a large ask that naturally splits into independent
pieces of work — do not implement it as one monolithic pass. Split it into separate commits, one
per feature/unit of work, and drive each unit through this graph-engineering framework using the
Agent tool:

```
Task -> Planner -> Worker -> [Reviewer 1, Reviewer 2, ... Reviewer N] -> Synthesise -> Pass?
                     ^                                                        |
                     |-------------------- feedback (no) ---------------------|
                                                                               |
                                                                          (yes) -> commit -> next unit
```

- **Planner**: breaks the overall ask into an ordered list of commit-sized units of work (a
  Plan Reviewer can review the plan itself before execution starts; route its feedback back to
  the Planner and send a summary of plan feedback to the user).
- **Worker**: a resident agent (kept alive across the reviewer round for a given unit) that
  implements one unit of work.
- **Reviewers (1..N)**: spawn multiple reviewer agents in parallel against the Worker's output —
  e.g. correctness, simplification/efficiency, and test coverage as separate reviewer passes.
  These can be ephemeral (fresh agent per round).
- **Synthesise**: reconcile the reviewers' findings into one set of required changes.
- **Pass? gate**: if synthesised feedback has no blocking issues, finalize and commit that unit
  with its own commit message, then move to the next planned unit. If it fails, send the
  synthesised feedback back to the Worker as another round on the same unit (don't restart from
  the Planner unless the feedback reveals the plan itself was wrong).

Net effect: one commit per feature/unit, each vetted by multiple reviewer passes before it lands,
rather than a single large uncommitted or unreviewed diff at the end.

## Verifying UI work: visual recreation (the main way to verify)

For any unit that changes UI, the primary verification is a **visual recreation**: render the real
components with mock data and look at a screenshot. Typecheck and unit tests are necessary but do not
count as verifying how it looks. Workers should do this before reporting, and I re-do it (or open the
image for the user) when the user asks to see it.

1. Add a **temporary** preview route (e.g. `apps/web/app/zz-preview/page.tsx`) that imports the real
   components and renders them with realistic mock props: populated, empty, capped/failed, long
   names/links. Put context around them (page background, a mock frame for panels/drawers that need a
   session or client state) but never reimplement the component itself.
2. Start the dev server in the background with dummy env vars the app needs to boot (e.g.
   `CONVEX_URL=https://dummy.convex.cloud CONVEX_DEPLOY_KEY=x NEXT_TELEMETRY_DISABLED=1 bunx next dev -p <port>`),
   wait for "Ready", and `curl` the route for a 200.
3. Screenshot with headless Chrome, not the preview MCP tools (those time out):
   `"/Applications/Google Chrome.app/Contents/MacOS/Google Chrome" --headless=new --disable-gpu --hide-scrollbars --force-device-scale-factor=2 --virtual-time-budget=6000 --window-size=<w>,<h> --screenshot=/tmp/<name>.png <url>`
   Take a wide desktop shot and a narrow one. Headless Chrome enforces a minimum window width, so a
   narrow shot can come out horizontally clipped; for true 320px checks render inside a 320px-wide
   iframe or measure element widths, and say so rather than treating clipping as a bug.
4. **Read the PNG** (the Read tool shows images) and actually look at it: hierarchy, spacing, truncation,
   overflow, alignment, tap targets, copy. Report what was seen versus what was not verified
   (hover/focus states, real clipboard/share, animations, Safari-only behavior, the real page behind auth).
5. For the user, `open` the desktop screenshot (copy it to `~/Downloads/<name>.png` first) since they
   can't see tool-output images.
6. **Clean up before committing**: stop the dev server (`pkill -f "next dev -p <port>"`), delete the
   preview route, temp public files and stray `.next` artifacts, and confirm `git status` shows only
   intended changes. Never commit a preview route or mocks.

# Mandatory visual + local-server verification (every agent, every run)

Applies to any task that changes code a user can see or that the running app depends on. No unit of
work is "done" until both of these have happened and been reported:

1. **Run it against the local server.** Start the real dev server (and `npx convex dev` when Convex
   code changed) in this worktree, wait for "Ready", and exercise the changed path end to end: `curl`
   the route for the expected status and hit changed API routes. A passing typecheck/lint/build alone
   does not count.
2. **Verify visually with a screenshot.** Follow the visual-recreation steps above (headless Chrome,
   wide + narrow shot), then Read the PNG and look at it. For pages behind auth, use a temporary
   preview route with mock data. Non-UI changes still get a screenshot of the affected page to prove
   nothing regressed.
3. **Report** what was seen, what was not verified (hover/focus, auth-gated pages, animations), and
   the screenshot path. If the server can't boot (e.g. missing env vars), say so explicitly and fix
   the env first (see below); never claim success without having run it.
4. Clean up (stop the server, delete preview routes/temp files) before committing.

Env vars: each worktree needs its own copy of the gitignored `.env*` files. If `.env.local` is
missing in the current worktree, symlink it from the canonical copy at `~/.config/avian/.env.local`
(`ln -s ~/.config/avian/.env.local .env.local`) before starting the server.

  implements one unit of work.
- **Reviewers (1..N)**: spawn multiple reviewer agents in parallel against the Worker's output —
  e.g. correctness, simplification/efficiency, and test coverage as separate reviewer passes.
  These can be ephemeral (fresh agent per round).
- **Synthesise**: reconcile the reviewers' findings into one set of required changes.
- **Pass? gate**: if synthesised feedback has no blocking issues, finalize and commit that unit
  with its own commit message, then move to the next planned unit. If it fails, send the
  synthesised feedback back to the Worker as another round on the same unit (don't restart from
  the Planner unless the feedback reveals the plan itself was wrong).

Net effect: one commit per feature/unit, each vetted by multiple reviewer passes before it lands,
rather than a single large uncommitted or unreviewed diff at the end.

## Verifying UI work: visual recreation (the main way to verify)

For any unit that changes UI, the primary verification is a **visual recreation**: render the real
components with mock data and look at a screenshot. Typecheck and unit tests are necessary but do not
count as verifying how it looks. Workers should do this before reporting, and I re-do it (or open the
image for the user) when the user asks to see it.

1. Add a **temporary** preview route (e.g. `apps/web/app/zz-preview/page.tsx`) that imports the real
   components and renders them with realistic mock props: populated, empty, capped/failed, long
   names/links. Put context around them (page background, a mock frame for panels/drawers that need a
   session or client state) but never reimplement the component itself.
2. Start the dev server in the background with dummy env vars the app needs to boot (e.g.
   `CONVEX_URL=https://dummy.convex.cloud CONVEX_DEPLOY_KEY=x NEXT_TELEMETRY_DISABLED=1 bunx next dev -p <port>`),
   wait for "Ready", and `curl` the route for a 200.
3. Screenshot with headless Chrome, not the preview MCP tools (those time out):
   `"/Applications/Google Chrome.app/Contents/MacOS/Google Chrome" --headless=new --disable-gpu --hide-scrollbars --force-device-scale-factor=2 --virtual-time-budget=6000 --window-size=<w>,<h> --screenshot=/tmp/<name>.png <url>`
   Take a wide desktop shot and a narrow one. Headless Chrome enforces a minimum window width, so a
   narrow shot can come out horizontally clipped; for true 320px checks render inside a 320px-wide
   iframe or measure element widths, and say so rather than treating clipping as a bug.
4. **Read the PNG** (the Read tool shows images) and actually look at it: hierarchy, spacing, truncation,
   overflow, alignment, tap targets, copy. Report what was seen versus what was not verified
   (hover/focus states, real clipboard/share, animations, Safari-only behavior, the real page behind auth).
5. For the user, `open` the desktop screenshot (copy it to `~/Downloads/<name>.png` first) since they
   can't see tool-output images.
6. **Clean up before committing**: stop the dev server (`pkill -f "next dev -p <port>"`), delete the
   preview route, temp public files and stray `.next` artifacts, and confirm `git status` shows only
   intended changes. Never commit a preview route or mocks.

# Mandatory visual + local-server verification (every agent, every run)

Applies to any task that changes code a user can see or that the running app depends on. No unit of
work is "done" until both of these have happened and been reported:

1. **Run it against the local server.** Start the real dev server (and `npx convex dev` when Convex
   code changed) in this worktree, wait for "Ready", and exercise the changed path end to end: `curl`
   the route for the expected status and hit changed API routes. A passing typecheck/lint/build alone
   does not count.
2. **Verify visually with a screenshot.** Follow the visual-recreation steps above (headless Chrome,
   wide + narrow shot), then Read the PNG and look at it. For pages behind auth, use a temporary
   preview route with mock data. Non-UI changes still get a screenshot of the affected page to prove
   nothing regressed.
3. **Report** what was seen, what was not verified (hover/focus, auth-gated pages, animations), and
   the screenshot path. If the server can't boot (e.g. missing env vars), say so explicitly and fix
   the env first (see below); never claim success without having run it.
4. Clean up (stop the server, delete preview routes/temp files) before committing.

Env vars: each worktree needs its own copy of the gitignored `.env*` files. If `.env.local` is
missing in the current worktree, symlink it from the canonical copy at `~/.config/avian/.env.local`
(`ln -s ~/.config/avian/.env.local .env.local`) before starting the server.
</system-reminder>

# BUILD_LOG

## Chunk 4: skeleton (models, state, runner, CLI, tracing)
- `agentbisect/models.py`: RegressionSpec, Plan(+Candidate), CommitResult, BisectState, CulpritReport, FixAttempt (JSON round-trip via `to_dict`/`from_dict`).
- `agentbisect/state.py`: `StateStore(.agentbisect/)` with atomic writes (tmp+fsync+rename), status transition table, `begin_step`/`end_step` (in-flight marker for crash resume), `log_context_tokens`, and `VerdictCache` keyed (repo, sha, case, agent_model, judge_model); build-failure skips cached too.
- `agentbisect/runner.py`: `Runner.evaluate_commit(sha, run_id)` -> `CommitResult`; detached git worktree (always cleaned), `uv sync` install (failure => `skip`), pluggable `EvalExecutor` (`SubprocessExecutor` runs `uv run python -m evals run --json --isolate --suite all --cases X --repeats N --commit SHA --run-id ID`, env `AGENTBISECT_*`), pinned-model enforcement (`ModelPinError`), bounded retry+backoff for rate limits/timeouts, parallel cases, confidence band (`good_min`/`bad_max`/`classify` hook) with repeat escalation to `max_repeats`, then verdict `flaky`.
- `agentbisect/cli.py`: `investigate`/`watch` stubs, `status`/`resume` work on state files. `agentbisect/tracing.py`: neatlogs workflow `agentbisect`, no-op without key.
- Tests: `uv run pytest` (21 pass; fake executors + throwaway git repo). No live model or neatlogs key was used; `SubprocessExecutor` is only tested against a stub `evals` package, not the real support-agent-demo.
- Eval secrets: worktrees lack gitignored `.env`; pass `RunnerConfig.env_file` or export keys in the environment.

## Chunk 5: intake
- `agentbisect/intake.py`: `TraceSource` ABC with `NeatlogsCliSource` (shells out to `~/.local/neatlogs-cli/bin/neatlogs --host https://app.neatlogs.com --profile neatlogs-us --credential-source profile --json [--project]`; `traces list|get|spans list|payload --fields input`, `detections get|hits|trends`) and `FixtureSource` (recorded JSON, can simulate auth failure). Auth failures (codes like UNAUTHENTICATED/TOKEN_EXPIRED or "not logged in"/401 text) raise `WaitingOnHumanLogin` (CLI exit 3) with the device-login command.
- Real CLI envelope is `{"data": {...}, "success": true}`; list items carry `traceId, workflowName, status, tags, startedAt`; tags are `commit:<sha>`, `case:<id>`, `run:<id>`. Project id needs `--project` or `NEATLOGS_PROJECT_ID`. Trace `input` is only available through span `payload --fields input`.
- `intake_trace`: bad trace -> case (case tag, else exact input match) -> good traces = same case, status not error, commit a strict ancestor of the bad commit (git), newest first, one per commit. Suite = non-held-out cases of that category; `held_out` = every case flagged `held_out` in the target's `evals/cases.jsonl` (an assert guards that the two never overlap; held-out checks are not in the predicate). Predicate = `{order: [checks, budget, rubric], checks per case, budget {max_steps 6, token_factor 1.5}, rubric per case or None}`. `breaks`/`intent_for` are never read.
- `intake_detection` (newest hit trace that maps to a case) and `intake_issue` (`gh issue view --json`, keyword->category match; optional injectable `LLM` interface called with the pinned `JUDGE_MODEL`, fake in tests, no live client shipped).
- CLI: `agentbisect investigate --trace|--detection|--issue --repo PATH [--fixtures F] [--project UUID]` writes the spec + good/bad sha into a new investigation; `agentbisect intake ...` prints it. `watch` still a stub.
- Tests: `tests/test_intake.py` (39 total pass). Live smoke: `list_traces`/`get_trace` against neatlogs worked (device login is done), but the project only holds synthetic probe traces (`commit:abc case:t1`), so real eval-trace mapping, `detections hits` item shape (no hits exist), pass/fail signal on real traces and span-level divergence are unverified.

## Chunk 6: plain bisect engine
- `agentbisect/bisect.py`: range resolution (bad = spec/`--bad`/HEAD, good = spec/`--good`; fails with a clear message if missing), `git rev-list --first-parent` history, both ends re-run once ("bad end does not reproduce", "good end is not good"). `narrow(history, results)` is a pure function of saved results (resume-safe); `PlainStrategy` binary-searches, skip/flaky commits count as tried so the nearest untested neighbour is picked (git bisect skip). Unresolvable => status `failed`, exit 4, "culprit is within these skipped/flaky commits: ..." (`metrics.ambiguous`).
- `Strategy` protocol (`next_commit(state)`, `update(state, sha, result)`) is the seam for chunk 7; `run_investigation(store, st, runner=None, strategy=None)`. Each evaluation is begin_step/end_step; `resume_investigation(store, st, runner=None, strategy=None)` returns the CLI exit code (0 ok, 1 error, 4 unresolved).
- After convergence one extra "monotonic probe" evaluates a commit between culprit and bad end; a good result (or any good-after-bad in cached verdicts) adds the warning "multiple regressions likely" and confidence `low`. Confidence: high (clean band, no skips/flaky), medium (inconclusive commits in range), low (non-monotonic). `metrics.confidence_band` holds the good/bad pass rates.
- `BisectState.metrics` (new): strategy, eval_rounds, cost_usd (eval_rounds x `AGENTBISECT_COST_PER_RUN`, default $0.002 estimate), commits_evaluated, cache_hits, warnings. Cache reuse across investigations comes from the runner's VerdictCache (second run on same repo = 0 eval rounds).
- CLI: `investigate ... --strategy plain [--good SHA] [--bad SHA]` runs end to end; `resume ID` calls the engine. Tests: `tests/test_bisect.py` (fake executor over a throwaway 14-commit repo: normal find at every position, skipped neighbours, skipped culprit-adjacent, flaky, crash+resume, non-monotonic, bad end not reproducing, cache reuse, custom strategy, CLI). 53 pass. Not run against the real support-agent-demo or live models.

## Chunk 7: smart planner
- `agentbisect/planner.py`: `first_divergence` (span diff -> `Plan.divergent_span`), `Planner` (graph impact -> commits touching impacted code -> checkpoint-intent ranking, each candidate `{sha, score, reason}`; score = 0.7 intent match + 0.3 code link), `SmartStrategy` (candidate, then its parent; clean candidate -> re-rank; nothing ranked left -> `PlainStrategy` on the open range, `metrics.planner.fell_back_to_plain`). Decisions are a pure function of the persisted plan + verdicts, so crash/resume re-uses the plan (no re-planning). `compare_strategies` + `agentbisect compare ID` run plain and smart in separate state dirs (empty caches) and print rounds/cost/context tokens.
- Scorers: deterministic `LexicalScorer` (idf-weighted term overlap) by default; `LLMScorer(llm)` takes any `intake.LLM` (no live client ships). No checkpoint -> commit message text (`reason` says `commit_message`).
- `intake.Span` + `TraceSource.spans()` (FixtureSource reads `"spans": {trace_id: [...]}`; `NeatlogsCliSource.spans` lists spans + `payload --fields output` to find chosen tools, real shape UNVERIFIED because the project has no real eval traces yet).
- CLI: `investigate --strategy smart|plain` (default smart, now runs the bisect; `--intake-only` for the old behaviour), `resume` rebuilds the strategy from `metrics.strategy`/`metrics.source`, `compare`.
- Real-tool findings (support-agent-demo, read-only): entire-graph WORKS for Python (`graph capabilities --json` lists Python as semantic). `graph impact --symbol S --repo . --format json --head --exclude-tests`: exact name -> `focus` + `callers.entries[].endpoint.file_path`; ambiguous/fuzzy -> `definitions[]` that include unrelated fuzzy hits (`S`, `one`) and tests, so the adapter keeps only definitions whose qualified name contains the symbol. Impact only sees the committed HEAD tree, not history. `graph commit <sha> --json` -> `files[].changes[{type, kind, name(qualified), dependents_count}]` works. `checkpoint explain <sha> --json` is metadata only (no intent text); intent needs `--full` (`[User]` block `Request:` line; `## Intent` is truncated with `...`; `## Summary` is a placeholder until generated). Commits with no trailer print "has no Entire-Checkpoint trailer" (rc 0); unknown sha rc 1.
- Dry check, real demo repo range 1041d3d..HEAD, hint `search_help`: graph found `ToolBox._tool_search_help` in tools/impl.py; planner read ~3.4KB of graph impact + ~63KB of checkpoint transcripts vs ~216KB estimated for the raw range diff + all intents. Unknown symbol -> graph returns only noise, planner flags `graph_empty`, uses git grep/-S and ranks by intent alone. Weakness: a tool-name hint only finds commits touching the tool file; regressions in loop/prompt code are reached by the plain fallback.
- Tests: `tests/test_planner.py` (fewer rounds than plain on a 30-commit repo, context tokens logged, clean-candidate re-rank, plain fallback, no-checkpoint, graph unavailable, skip, crash/resume, parsers on real output shapes, CLI/compare). 67 pass. No live model or neatlogs call.

## Chunk 8: culprit analyst + revert test
- `agentbisect/culprit.py`: `analyze_culprit` -> `CulpritReport` (checkpoint prompt + reasoning parsed from `entire checkpoint explain --full`, commit-message fallback flagged `no checkpoint`; semantic diff from `entire graph diff --base <sha>~1 --head <sha> --json` + callers via `graph impact`, fallback `git show --stat` + hunk-header symbols; span-by-span good/bad trace divergence; failing evidence). `fixer_brief` = culprit diff + labelled ORIGINAL INTENT + failing evidence only (no log, no other commits). Verified on real support-agent-demo checkpoint/graph output (read-only).
- `agentbisect/verify.py`: `revert_test` builds HEAD-with-culprit-reverted in a fresh worktree (`git revert --no-commit`, snapshotted as a deterministic throwaway commit so Runner/cache/pins are reused and resume is safe), runs the suite cases, passes when the pass rate returns to the good-commit level minus 0.1. Conflicts: abort, retry with only the hunks that still reverse-apply (`git apply -R --reject`); flag `revert conflicts`, confidence down one notch; nothing applicable or unbuildable -> inconclusive (`None`). Revert not fixing -> confidence `low` + `multiple regressions likely` flag/warning. Eval rounds recorded in `metrics.revert_test` and added to `eval_rounds`/cost. Fix-verification hooks left for chunk 11.
- Flow: `investigate`/`resume` run `confirm_culprit` after a bisect culprit (resume-safe, idempotent, status stays `culprit_found`); `status` shows culprit, revert result, rates, intent source, flags. `CulpritReport` gained optional fields (intent_source, trace_divergence, failing_evidence, flags, revert_details, analyzed); `_conclude` keeps an existing analysed culprit on resume.
- Tests: `tests/test_culprit.py` (normal pass, wrong culprit, conflict inconclusive, partial revert, unbuildable, deterministic commit, no-checkpoint, graph diff, trace divergence, Fixer brief isolation, status). 79 pass. No live model/neatlogs call; no UI so no screenshot.

## Chunk 9: reporter
- `agentbisect/report.py`: `build_report(state)` -> one dict rendered by `render_markdown` / `render_html` (self-contained, inline CSS, everything html-escaped; Markdown fences widen past backticks in untrusted text). Sections: culprit, labelled original intent (checkpoint vs "NO CHECKPOINT" commit-message fallback), semantic diff + symbols, trace divergence, revert test, confidence + "multiple regressions likely" warning, smart-vs-plain (from `metrics.comparison`, now saved by `agentbisect compare`), fix section ("not attempted" without a FixAttempt; "NOT verified" draft variant when the best attempt misses baseline-0.1 or the intent test), context tokens per step, commits table, trace ids + links, Entire checkpoint ids (git trailer, best effort) + `entire checkpoint explain <sha> --full`.
- `open_pr(state, repo, draft=None, confirm=False, run=...)`: DRY-RUN by default (prints title/body/`git push` + `gh pr create`); only `--open-pr --confirm-open-pr` executes; body ends with the Claude Code line. Tests inject a stub runner, nothing is pushed. After a confirmed PR the status becomes `reported`.
- CLI: `agentbisect report ID [--format md|html|both] [--out DIR] [--open-pr --confirm-open-pr] [--draft]`; default out dir is `evidence/` in this repo.
- UNVERIFIED: the neatlogs trace URL pattern (`https://app.neatlogs.com/traces/{trace_id}`, override `AGENTBISECT_NEATLOGS_TRACE_URL`); only the host is documented. Real `gh pr create` never run. Fix-stage state (chunk 11) may need to supply `FixAttempt` fields as modelled.
- Tests: `tests/test_report.py`; 87 pass. Visual check: static HTML (no dev server) rendered with headless Chrome at wide and 360px-iframe; layout read OK.

## Chunk 10a: claude-CLI LLM proxy (subscription backend)
- `agentbisect/llm_proxy.py` + `agentbisect llm-proxy [--port 8787] [--concurrency 3] [--cache]`: stdlib `ThreadingHTTPServer` serving `POST /v1/messages` (non-streaming; stream=true -> 400), `GET /stats`, `GET /health`. Each call shells out to `claude -p --model <exact id> --output-format json --tools "" --system-prompt ... --setting-sources "" --strict-mcp-config --no-session-persistence` in an empty temp cwd. Credentials are never read; only the binary is run.
- Tool use is emulated: schemas + conversation (incl. tool_use/tool_result history) rendered into the prompt, `--json-schema` forces `{text, tool_calls[{name,input}]}`; output validated against the supplied input_schemas (retry once with the error, then 502 Anthropic-style error); blocks get `toolu_*` ids, stop_reason tool_use/end_turn. The prompt must say outright that tools are available (first attempt made Haiku claim it had no tools).

Rate limits (is_error/api_error_status 429/529 or text match) retry with exponential backoff, then HTTP 429 + `retry-after` so SDK retries behave. Semaphore caps concurrency. Optional cache `.agentbisect/llm_cache` keyed by sha256(model, system, messages, tools, tool_choice).
- LIMITS: temperature cannot be set (logged in /stats `temperatures`, otherwise ignored), so runs are not temperature-0 deterministic. Input tokens include ~1.2k of CLI overhead per call plus the emulated tool prompt (~6k per tool turn with the demo's schemas), so token budgets are inflated but consistent; do not compare against raw API counts. ~3-8 s per call.
- Runner: `RunnerConfig.llm_proxy_url` (default `$AGENTBISECT_LLM_PROXY_URL`) sets `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` and dummy `REDACTED` in the eval env. `investigate --llm-proxy auto|URL|off`: auto starts an in-process proxy (cache on) for the run, prints stats on exit.
- Tests: `tests/test_llm_proxy.py` with a fake `claude` script on PATH (plain text, tool call, multi-turn, invalid retry x2, 429 backoff/exhaustion, concurrency cap, cache hit, model pin, stats, stream, runner env). 98 pass.

Whole session: ~12 live calls, ~$0.008 list-price equivalent.

## Chunk 10b: os1 fail at HEAD was a proxy artifact (ambient user context)
- Symptom: os1-os3 failed reply_contains at demo HEAD ("order 1042 isn't linked to your account, I can't share its details"). Cause: `claude -p` injects the logged-in user's own context ("The user's email address is ...") into every call; `--system-prompt`, `--setting-sources ""` and `--exclude-dynamic-system-prompt-sections` do not remove it, `--bare` cannot use the login. The model compared that email with `customer_email` in the tool result and refused. One reply even quoted the user's email. The rendered tool_result prompt was complete and untruncated (checked via the new dump).
- Fix: `ISOLATION_NOTICE` appended to every system prompt. `agentbisect llm-proxy --debug-dump DIR` (use /tmp) writes each rendered system/prompt/output for debugging; it contains full prompts, so debug only.
- Evidence (haiku-5-5, live): before fix HEAD os1-3 0/3, mid (96de44a) 0/3, baseline (1041d3d) 1/3. After fix HEAD 9/9 (3 each of os1-3), though os1 now calls search_help too (prompt rule "verify with search_help" from 59c8b10; a budget issue, not a check failure).

The signature comes from trace hints (`failed_checks` metadata / `check:` tag, none exist on real neatlogs traces yet) or is discovered at the bad end (`_discover_signature`; deterministic check preferred over budget, bad trace's case preferred). """Failure signatures: the specific failing check behind a bad run, so the bisect predicate can be "does THIS
signature reproduce?" instead of "does the case fail?".

A harness result (support-agent-demo `evals` schema_version 1) lists `checks: [{check, passed, reason}]`, a `budget`
block and an optional `judge` block. Each failed one becomes a failure record {key, check, detail, expected, got,
reason}; `key` is the identity used to match runs and commits:

  call_args:<tool>.<arg>   a tool call whose argument is wrong (expected/got parsed from the check reason)
  budget:steps|tokens      step or token budget exceeded
  judge                    rubric failed
  <check name>             any other deterministic check (reply_regex, must_call, ...)

Other failures (e.g. a budget regression elsewhere) are simply different keys and count as a pass for this one.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import ast
import re
from collections import defaultdict
from typing import Any, Iterable

from .models import BisectState, CommitResult, FailureSignature
from .state import StateStore

_CALL_ARGS = re.compile(r"no (\w+) call matching (\{.*?\}) \(saw (\[.*?\])\)(?:;|$)", re.S)


def _num(v: Any) -> float | None:
    return float(v) if isinstance(v, (int, float)) and not isinstance(v, bool) else None


def _same(a: Any, b: Any) -> bool:
    x, y = _num(a), _num(b)
    return abs(x - y) <= 0.005 if x is not None and y is not None else a == b


def _call_args_failures(reason: str) -> list[dict[str, str]]:
    out = []
    for tool, want_s, saw_s in _CALL_ARGS.findall(reason):
        try:
            want, saw = ast.literal_eval(want_s), ast.literal_eval(saw_s)
        except (ValueError, SyntaxError):
            out.append({"key": f"call_args:{tool}", "detail": tool, "expected": "", "got": ""})
            continue
        if not saw:
            out.append({"key": f"call_args:{tool}", "detail": tool, "expected": "a call", "got": "no call"})
            continue
        bad = [k for k, v in want.items() if not any(_same(c.get(k), v) for c in saw)]
        for k in bad or list(want):
            out.append({"key": f"call_args:{tool}.{k}", "detail": f"{tool}.{k}", "expected": str(want[k]),
                        "got": str(saw[0].get(k))})
    return out


def failure_records(check: str, reason: str) -> list[dict[str, str]]:
    base = {"check": check, "reason": reason[:300]}
    if check == "call_args":
        recs = _call_args_failures(reason)
        if recs:
            return [{**base, **r} for r in recs]
    return [{**base, "key": check, "detail": "", "expected": "", "got": ""}]


def failures_of_result(r: dict[str, Any]) -> list[dict[str, str]]:
    """Failure records for one harness result dict (empty for passing runs). A failing run with no recorded
    cause still gets a generic `case_fail` record so it is never silently treated as a pass."""
    out: list[dict[str, str]] = []
    for c in r.get("checks") or []:
        if not c.get("passed", True):
            out += failure_records(str(c.get("check")), str(c.get("reason") or ""))
    b = r.get("budget") or {}
    if b.get("status") == "fail":
        reason = str(b.get("reason") or "")
        kinds = [k for k in ("steps", "tokens") if k in reason] or ["steps"]
        out += [{"key": f"budget:{k}", "check": "budget", "detail": k, "expected": "", "got": "",
                 "reason": reason[:300]} for k in kinds]
    j = r.get("judge")
    if isinstance(j, dict) and j.get("passed") is False:
        out.append({"key": "judge", "check": "judge", "detail": "", "expected": "", "got": "",
                    "reason": str(j.get("reason") or "")[:300]})
    if not out and r.get("status") == "fail":
        out.append({"key": "case_fail", "check": "case_fail", "detail": "", "expected": "", "got": "",
                    "reason": str(r.get("reason") or "")[:300]})
    return out


def signature_from_record(rec: dict[str, str]) -> FailureSignature:
    return FailureSignature(key=rec["key"], check=rec.get("check", ""), detail=rec.get("detail", ""),
                            expected=rec.get("expected", ""), got=rec.get("got", ""), reason=rec.get("reason", ""))


def signature_from_key(key: str) -> FailureSignature:
    """For `--signature KEY` on the command line."""
    check, _, detail = key.partition(":")
    return FailureSignature(key=key, check=check, detail=detail)


def signatures_of(result: CommitResult) -> list[FailureSignature]:
    """All failing checks seen at a commit, one signature each, most frequent first."""
    sigs = [FailureSignature.from_dict(d) for d in result.failure_signatures]
    return sorted(sigs, key=lambda s: (-s.fails, s.key))


def group_signatures(infos: dict[str, dict[str, Any]], case_runs: dict[str, int],
                     case_fails: dict[str, dict[str, int]]) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
    """infos: key -> first-seen record; case_fails: case -> {key: failing runs}; case_runs: case -> executed runs.
    -> signature dicts with the cases where the key fires and run counts over those cases."""
    by_key: dict[str, list[str]] = defaultdict(list)
    for case, ks in case_fails.items():
        for k, n in ks.items():
            if n > 0:
                by_key[k].append(case)
    out = []
    for k, cases in by_key.items():
        cases = sorted(cases)
        s = signature_from_record(infos.get(k) or {"key": k})
        s.cases = cases
        s.fails = sum(case_fails[c][k] for c in cases)
        s.runs = sum(case_runs.get(c, 0) for c in cases)
        out.append(s.to_dict())
    return out


def pick_primary(sigs: Iterable[FailureSignature], bad_case: str | None) -> FailureSignature | None:
    """The signature to bisect first: one that fires in the bad trace's case, else any. A wrong behaviour (a
    deterministic check) outranks a cost miss (budget), since the report of a bad trace is about wrong output;
    then the most frequent. The others are bisected as siblings."""
    sigs = sorted(sigs, key=lambda s: (s.check == "budget", s.check == "judge", -s.fails, s.key))
    if bad_case:
        mine = [s for s in sigs if bad_case in s.cases]
        if mine:
            return mine[0]
    return sigs[0] if sigs else None


def signature_from_trace(metadata: dict[str, Any], tags: list[str]) -> FailureSignature | None:
    """A trace that carries its own failing check: metadata `failed_checks` ([{check, reason}]) or a
    `check:<key>` tag. Real neatlogs traces do not carry this today; the bad end's eval result is used then."""
    for fc in metadata.get("failed_checks") or []:
        if isinstance(fc, dict) and fc.get("check"):
            return signature_from_record(failure_records(str(fc["check"]), str(fc.get("reason") or ""))[0])
    for t in tags:
        if t.startswith("check:") and len(t) > 6:
            return signature_from_key(t[6:])
    return None


# -- planner feed --

def symptom_text(sig: FailureSignature) -> str:
    """Words for the planner's intent scoring."""
    if sig.check == "case_fail":  # no specific check known: nothing to add to the symptom
        return ""
    bits = [sig.check, sig.detail.replace(".", " ").replace("_", " "), sig.reason]
    if sig.expected or sig.got:
        bits += [f"expected {sig.expected}", f"got {sig.got}"]
    e, g = _try_float(sig.expected), _try_float(sig.got)
    if e and g and (abs(g / e - 100) < 1e-6 or abs(g / e - 0.01) < 1e-9):  # 64.0 vs 6400: a units mix-up
        bits.append("cents dollars unit conversion")
    return " ".join(b for b in bits if b)


def _try_float(v: str) -> float | None:
    try:
        return float(v)
    except (TypeError, ValueError):
        return None


def symbol_hints(sig: FailureSignature) -> list[str]:
    """Names to look up with `entire graph impact`: the tool behind a call_args failure, plus refund/amount
    vocabulary when the failing value is a money amount."""
    hints: list[str] = []
    if sig.check == "call_args" and sig.detail:
        tool = sig.detail.split(".")[0]
        hints += [tool, f"_tool_{tool}"]
    text = f"{sig.detail} {sig.reason}".lower()
    hints += [w for w in ("refund", "amount") if w in text]
    return list(dict.fromkeys(hints))


# -- overlapping regressions: one investigation per signature --

def spawn_siblings(store: StateStore, st: BisectState) -> list[BisectState]:
    """After the primary investigation discovered several failing checks at the bad end, create one more
    investigation per remaining signature (same repo, range, strategy; shared verdict cache, so commits already
    evaluated for the cases they share cost nothing). Idempotent: siblings are recorded on the primary."""
    from .models import RegressionSpec
    found = [FailureSignature.from_dict(d) for d in st.metrics.get("signatures", [])]
    mine = st.spec.signature.key if st.spec and st.spec.signature else None
    done = {x["key"]: x["id"] for x in st.metrics.get("signature_siblings", [])}
    made = []
    for sig in found:
        if sig.key == mine or sig.key in done:
            continue
        spec = RegressionSpec.from_dict({**st.spec.to_dict(), "signature": sig.to_dict()})
        sib = store.create(st.repo, spec=spec, good_sha=st.good_sha, bad_sha=st.bad_sha)
        sib.metrics.update(strategy=st.metrics.get("strategy", "plain"), source=st.metrics.get("source"),
                           signature_group=st.id, signatures_discovered=True)
        store.save(sib)
        st.metrics.setdefault("signature_siblings", []).append({"id": sib.id, "key": sig.key})
        made.append(sib)
    store.save(st)
    return made

def _discover_signature(store: StateStore, st: BisectState, runner: Runner, bad: str) -> None:
    """Pick the failing check to bisect on, once: evaluate the bad end over the whole suite, group every failing
    check into signatures (all kept in metrics["signatures"]) and bisect the one that fires in the bad trace's
    case. Skipped when intake already supplied a signature or it was discovered before (resume-safe)."""
    if not st.spec or st.spec.signature is not None or st.metrics.get("signatures_discovered"):
        runner.signature = st.spec.signature if st.spec else None
        return
    step = store.begin_step(st, "signature_discovery", sha=bad)
    before = runner.eval_rounds
    runner.signature = None
    with step_span("signature_discovery", sha=bad, step=step):
        res = runner.evaluate_commit(bad, f"{st.id}-s{step}", list(st.spec.cases))
    _account(st, runner.eval_rounds - before)
    sigs = signatures_of(res)
    st.metrics["signatures_discovered"] = True
    st.metrics["signatures"] = [s.to_dict() for s in sigs]
    st.spec.signature = runner.signature = pick_primary(sigs, st.spec.bad_case)
    if st.spec.signature is None:
        st.metrics.setdefault("warnings", []).append(
            "no failing check found at the bad end: bisecting on whole-case pass rate")
    store.end_step(st)


def _evaluate(store: StateStore, st: BisectState, runner: Runner, sha: str, kind: str) -> CommitResult:
    step = store.begin_step(st, kind, sha=sha)
    before = runner.eval_rounds
    with step_span("bisect_step", sha=sha, step=step, kind=kind):
        res = runner.evaluate_commit(sha, f"{st.id}-s{step}")
    m = st.metrics
    _account(st, runner.eval_rounds - before)
    m["commits_evaluated"] = m.get("commits_evaluated", 0) + (0 if res.from_cache else 1)
    m["cache_hits"] = m.get("cache_hits", 0) + (1 if res.from_cache else 0)
    store.end_step(st, sha, res)
    return res


def _fail(store: StateStore, st: BisectState, msg: str) -> Outcome:
    store.set_status(st, "failed", error=msg)
    return Outcome("failed", message=msg)


def _confirm_ends(store: StateStore, st: BisectState, runner: Runner, good: str, bad: str) -> str | None:
    """Re-run both ends once (cached verdicts count). Returns an error message or None."""
    for sha, want, label in ((bad, "bad", "bad end"), (good, "good", "good end")):
        res = st.results.get(sha)
        if res is None or res.verdict == "skip":
            res = _evaluate(store, st, runner, sha, f"confirm_{want}")
        if res.verdict != want:
            if want == "bad" and res.verdict == "good":
                sig = f" for signature {st.spec.signature.key}" if st.spec and st.spec.signature else ""
                return f"bad end does not reproduce{sig}: {sha[:8]} passes (pass_rate {res.pass_rate:.2f})"
            if want == "good" and res.verdict == "bad":
                return f"good end is not good: {sha[:8]} fails (pass_rate {res.pass_rate:.2f})"
            return f"{label} {sha[:8]} is unusable: verdict {res.verdict} ({res.reason})"
    return None


def _confidence(history: list[str], st: BisectState, n: Narrowing) -> tuple[str, dict]:
    lo_r, hi_r = st.results[history[n.lo]], st.results[history[n.hi]]
    band = {"good_pass_rate": lo_r.pass_rate, "bad_pass_rate": hi_r.pass_rate}
    inconclusive = [h for h in history if (r := st.results.get(h)) and r.verdict in ("skip", "flaky")]
    if n.non_monotonic:
        return "low", band

class OverlapExec:
    """Commit idx >= 3 adds R2 (budget failure in every case); idx >= 8 adds R3 (refund amount wrong in a and b)."""

    def __init__(self):
        self.runs = 0

    def run_case(self, req):
        idx = int((req.workdir / "marker.txt").read_text())
        out = []
        for i in range(req.repeats):
            self.runs += 1
            fails = []
            if idx >= 3:
                fails.append(BUDGET)
            if idx >= 8 and req.case in ("a", "b"):
                fails.append(AMOUNT)
            out.append(RunResult(req.case, "fail" if fails else "pass", trace_id=f"t{idx}-{req.case}-{i}",
                                 agent_model=PINS["agent_model"], judge_model=PINS["judge_model"], failures=fails))
        return out


def make(tmp_path, hist, spec=None, ex=None):
    repo, shas = hist
    store = StateStore(tmp_path / "ab")
    runner = Runner(repo, RunnerConfig(cases=["a", "b", "c"], repeats=2, install_cmd=None, models=dict(PINS),
                                       backoff=0.0), store.cache(str(repo)), ex or OverlapExec(),
                    sleep=lambda s: None)
    st = store.create(str(repo), spec=spec or RegressionSpec(cases=["a", "b", "c"], bad_case="a"),
                      good_sha=shas[0], bad_sha=shas[-1])
    return store, runner, st, shas


def test_bisects_on_signature_not_case(tmp_path, hist):
    store, runner, st, shas = make(tmp_path, hist)
    out = B.run_investigation(store, st, runner)
    st = store.load(st.id)
    # the bad trace is in case a, whose amount failure starts at 8, although the case already fails from 3 (budget)
    assert out.kind == "culprit" and out.sha == shas[8]
    assert st.spec.signature.key == "call_args:issue_refund.amount" and st.spec.signature.cases == ["a", "b"]
    assert {d["key"] for d in st.metrics["signatures"]} == {"call_args:issue_refund.amount", "budget:steps"}
    mid = [r for sha, r in st.results.items() if shas.index(sha) in range(3, 8)]
    assert mid and all(r.verdict == "good" for r in mid)  # R2's budget failures count as a pass for this signature


def test_all_signatures_gives_one_culprit_each_and_shares_cache(tmp_path, hist):
    ex = OverlapExec()
    store, runner, st, shas = make(tmp_path, hist, ex=ex)
    B.run_investigation(store, st, runner)
    st = store.load(st.id)
    sibs = S.spawn_siblings(store, st)
    assert [s.spec.signature.key for s in sibs] == ["budget:steps"]
    assert S.spawn_siblings(store, store.load(st.id)) == []  # idempotent
    sib = store.load(sibs[0].id)
    r2 = Runner(st.repo, RunnerConfig(cases=["a", "b", "c"], repeats=2, install_cmd=None, models=dict(PINS)),
                store.cache(st.repo), ex, signature=sib.spec.signature, sleep=lambda s: None)
    out = B.run_investigation(store, sib, r2)
    assert out.sha == shas[3]

    assert sib.metrics["signature_group"] == st.id

entries.name: Monitor
entries.description:
Start a background monitor that streams events from a long-running script. Each stdout line is an event — you keep working and notifications arrive in the chat. Events arrive on their own schedule and are not replies from the user, even if one lands while you're waiting for the user to answer a question.

Pick by how many notifications you need:
- **One** ("tell me when the server is ready / the build finishes") → use **Bash with `run_in_background`** and a command that exits when the condition is true, e.g. `until grep -q "Ready in" dev.log; do sleep 0.5; done`. You get a single completion notification when it exits.
- **One per occurrence, until the monitor expires (re-arm to continue)** ("tell me every time an ERROR line appears") → Monitor with an unbounded command (`tail -f`, `inotifywait -m`, `while true`).
- **One per occurrence, until a known end** ("emit each CI step result, stop when the run completes") → Monitor with a command that emits lines and then exits.

Your script's stdout is the event stream. Each line becomes a notification. Exit ends the watch.

  # Each matching log line is an event
  tail -f /var/log/app.log | grep --line-buffered "ERROR"

  # Each file change is an event
  inotifywait -m --format '%e %f' /watched/dir

  # Poll GitHub for new PR comments and emit one line per new comment
  last=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)
  while true; do
    now=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)
    gh api "repos/owner/repo/issues/123/comments?since=$last" --jq '.[] | "\(.user.login): \(.body)"'
    last=$now; sleep 30
  done

  # Node script that emits events as they arrive (e.g. WebSocket listener)
  node watch-for-events.js

  # Per-occurrence with a natural end: emit each CI check as it lands, exit when the run completes
  prev=""
  while true; do
    s=$(gh pr checks 123 --json name,bucket)
    cur=$(jq -r '.[] | select(.bucket!="pending") | "\(.name): \(.bucket)"' <<<"$s" | sort)
    comm -13 <(echo "$prev") <(echo "$cur")
    prev=$cur
    jq -e 'all(.bucket!="pending")' <<<"$s" >/dev/null && break
    sleep 30
  done

**Don't use an unbounded command for a single notification.** `tail -f`, `inotifywait -m`, and `while true` never exit on their own, so the monitor stays armed until timeout even after the event has fired. For "tell me when X is ready," use Bash `run_in_background` with an `until` loop instead (one notification, ends in seconds). Note that `tail -f log | grep -m 1 ...` does *not* fix this: if the log goes quiet after the match, `tail` never receives SIGPIPE and the pipeline hangs anyway.

**Script quality:**
- Every pipe stage must flush per line or matches sit in its buffer unseen: `grep` needs `--line-buffered`, `awk` needs `fflush()`. `head` cannot flush at all — `| head -N` delivers nothing until N matches accumulate, then ends the stream.
- In poll loops, handle transient failures (`curl ... || true`) — one failed request shouldn't kill the monitor.
- Poll intervals: 30s+ for remote APIs (rate limits), 0.5-1s for local checks.
- Write a specific `description` — it appears in every notification ("errors in deploy.log" not "watching logs").
- Only stdout is the event stream. Stderr goes to the output file (readable via Read) but does not trigger notifications — for a command you run directly (e.g. `python train.py 2>&1 | grep --line-buffered ...`), merge stderr with `2>&1` so its failures reach your filter. (No effect on `tail -f` of an existing log — that file only contains what its writer redirected.)

**Coverage — silence is not success.** When watching a job or process for an outcome, your filter must match every terminal state, not just the happy path. A monitor that greps only for the success marker stays silent through a crashloop, a hung process, or an unexpected exit — and silence looks identical to "still running." Before arming, ask: *if this process crashed right now, would my filter emit anything?* If not, widen it.

  # Wrong — silent on crash, hang, or any non-success exit
  tail -f run.log | grep --line-buffered "elapsed_steps="

  # Right — one alternation covering progress + the failure signatures you'd act on
  tail -f run.log | grep -E --line-buffered "elapsed_steps=|Traceback|Error|FAILED|assert|Killed|OOM"

For poll loops checking job state, emit on every terminal status (`succeeded|failed|cancelled|timeout`), not just success. If you cannot confidently enumerate the failure signatures, broaden the grep alternation rather than narrow it — some extra noise is better than missing a crashloop.

**Output volume**: Every stdout line is a conversation message, so the filter should be selective — but selective means "the lines you'd act on," not "only good news." Never pipe raw logs; filter to exactly the success and failure signals you care about. Monitors that produce too many events are automatically stopped; restart with a tighter filter if this happens.

Stdout lines within 200ms are batched into a single notification, so multiline output from a single event groups naturally.

The script runs in the same shell environment as Bash. Exit ends the watch (exit code is reported). Every monitor expires after `timeout_ms` (default 5 minutes, at most 30 minutes): it is killed and you get one notice with the event count. Re-arm it if you still need the watch; for a long watch (PR monitoring, log tails) set `timeout_ms` to the maximum and re-arm on each expiry, and widen the filter if an expiry with no events was unexpected. Use TaskStop to cancel early.
**ws source** — open a WebSocket and stream each incoming text frame as an event. No shell, no polling: the server pushes, you get notified.

  Monitor({
    ws: {url: 'wss://events.example.com/stream', protocols: ['v1']},
    description: 'deploy events',
  })

Each text frame becomes one notification (multiline frames stay as one event). Binary frames are reported as `[binary frame, N bytes]` rather than passed through. Socket close ends the watch with the close code surfaced; errors are surfaced before close. Same rate limiting as bash — a firehose will be suppressed and eventually stopped, so subscribe to a filtered feed where one exists.

Prefer this over `command: 'websocat wss://…'` — it avoids the extra process and line-buffering pitfalls. Use bash when you need to transform or filter frames with shell tools before they become events.

description.description: Short human-readable description of what you are monitoring (shown in notifications).

timeout_ms.description: Kill the monitor after this deadline. Default 300000ms. Deadlines above 1800000ms are capped to 1800000ms. You are notified at expiry and can re-arm.

command.description: Shell command or script. Each stdout line is an event; exit ends the watch.

ws.description: WebSocket to open. Each text frame is an event; binary frames are reported as a placeholder line. Socket close ends the watch. Cannot be combined with command.

content.thinking:
I'm thinking through a minimal fix: when the good end's evaluation comes back as "skip: no executed runs," I need a helper that advances the good commit forward through history, repeatedly evaluating each candidate until it finds one that actually has executed runs.

If the next executable commit is already bad, the real question becomes whether a skip at the good end — where the signature's cases are simply absent — should count as vacuously good. If so, bisection can proceed over the range treating skipped commits as inconclusive neighbors, with the eventual culprit being the first commit where the cases become executable and bad.

I think the cleanest fix is in evaluate_commit: when there are zero passes/fails but every relevant case is target-skipped (not errored), I'll mark it as a "good" verdict with pass_rate 1.0 and a reason noting the cases aren't applicable at that commit. I'll scope this only to when a signature is active, so it doesn't risk masking genuine build-wide skips in the non-signature flow.

| signature | culprit found | verdict | revert test |
|---|---|---|---|

content.text:
Only R3 came out cleanly; R1 and R2 did not get their own culprit with a passing revert test. I pushed everything to origin main (HEAD `4f05452`).

**Setup:** good `1b40b27`, bad `f7d82b7`, DEMO_FLAKE=0, haiku agent and sonnet judge through the llm-proxy. At `1b40b27` the quick eval passed 18 of 19 executed cases. `es2` fails there too, and the cancel_order cases are skipped because the tool doesn't exist yet. I had to calibrate a token baseline first: without one the harness skips token budgets, and R1/R2 only show up as budget failures.

**Scoring caveat:** `ground_truth.json` maps cases to regressions, not to culprit commits. R1/R2 scoring below rests on case mapping and commit messages only.

| Signature | Culprit | Scored against ground truth |
|---|---|---|
| R3: `call_args:issue_refund.amount` | `b0be626` (cents) | Correct; revert test passed (0% to 100%) |
| `budget:tokens@refund_within_policy` | `59c8b10` | Plausibly R2's commit, but revert failed (50% to 50%) |
| `budget:tokens@order_status` (R1 cases) | `59c8b10` | Not a separate R1 culprit; revert failed |
| `budget:tokens@policy_question` (R2 cases) | `f7d82b7` | Wrong, borderline noise at the last commit |
| `budget:tokens@escalation` (R2 cases) | `ca150c7` | Wrong or unconfirmed; revert failed |
| `budget:tokens@cancel_request` | `96de44a` | Unverified (revert inconclusive) |
| `budget:tokens@multi_step` | `22f7fbd` | Unverified, one case, one sample |
| `call_args:escalate_to_human.priority` | none | Correctly refused: `es2` fails at the good end too |

**Why R1 and R2 didn't separate:** the token regressions inflate every category, so per-category signatures still mix them. With one repeat per case, verdicts near the 1.5x limit flip.

**Rounds:**
- **R3 investigation:** 43 eval rounds including signature discovery.
- **Smart vs plain (`compare`):** R3 took 21 vs 24 rounds and the order_status budget 24 vs 27. Both found the same culprit. Planner context was 21.7k vs 43.3k tokens with the graph.
- **Across all 8 investigations:** about 125 eval rounds.

**Throttling:** across 1417 proxy calls there were 0 rate-limit, backoff, recovered or gave-up events. The live backoff path is still only tested with fakes.

**Bugs found and fixed:** one commit each; 146 tests pass, and the first fix passed a reviewer.
1. Budget regressions in different features collapsed into one signature.
   - The suite covered only the trace's category.
   - One flaky `rw3` run spawned three noise siblings.
   - **Fix:** budget keys are now `budget:tokens@<category>`, there is an `--all-categories` flag, and a signature seen in only one run is re-run and dropped if it doesn't reproduce.
   - **Reviewer:** it caught three problems, which I fixed.
2. Signatures whose cases don't exist at the good end (the cancel_order cases) made that end unusable. They now count as vacously good. I resumed the two affected siblings; the other six ran before this fix.

**Unverified:**
- Span divergence (neatlogs dead-letter).
- Multi-repeat budget stability (I never tried raising the repeat count).
- Haiku non-determinism.

Everything is in `/Users/jaxson/Downloads/codingprojects/agentbisect/evidence/`:
- `rerun-summary.md` has the numbers and caveats.
- `report-*.md` and `report-*.html` cover the 8 investigations.
- `rerun1-prefix/` has the pre-fix run.
- `rerun2-investigate.log` and `rerun2-compare.log` are the raw output.
- `rerun2-baseline.json` is the baseline.

`BUILD_LOG.md` is updated.
